parsed.explanation: The quoted passage asserts the crucial halving estimate. The stated facts—that the uncancelled totals sum to T-d and that the rows interchange at one cut—do not imply that each total is at most (T-d)/2; the sum condition alone allows one total to exceed half. The proof also does not derive the claimed bound of s column-blocks or explain why recursively controlling only the odd array controls the entire odd-level integral in (5). No later argument repairs these gaps: Section 4 invokes Lemma (i) directly. Thus the all-n upper bound is not established as written.
